territorial_scope.description: Applies to sales tax on transactions within North Dakota, under the state sales tax chapter.

evidence.quote: Gross receipts from sales of enterprise information technology equipment and computer software purchased for use by a qualifying business in a qualified data center are exempt from the tax imposed by this chapter.

summary.short: North Dakota sales and use tax exemption for enterprise information technology equipment and computer software bought for use in a certified qualified data center. Covers owners, operators and tenants, with a certification step and annual reporting to the tax commissioner.
summary.long: Exempts from North Dakota sales and use tax the gross receipts from sales of enterprise information technology equipment and computer software purchased for use by a qualifying business in a qualified data center, including upgraded or replacement equipment. A future owner must apply to the tax commissioner for certification and answer information requests within thirty days. The exemption requires a commissioner certificate at purchase; otherwise the business pays the tax and applies for a refund, and contractor-installed purchases may be refunded. A qualified data center is a newly constructed or substantially refurbished facility of at least 15,000 square feet, at least half used for data processing, on one or contiguous parcels, with construction completed after December 31, 2020, sophisticated fire suppression, enhanced security features, and commissioner certification. Owners must give collocated operators or tenants documentation of certification. By January 31 each year the owner files a report of the exemption claimed, jobs created or retained, and local incentives. The commissioner may disclose these report details to legislative management chairs on written request, excluding the owner's name and identifiers. Heading notes retroactive application.

notes: Only the section 57-39.2-04.17 is annotated although the document is the full chapter. The heading carries '(Retroactive application - See note)' but no note text appears in the document. The text gives no enacting session law, amendment or repeal for this section, so no legal_basis, amends or repeals relations are recorded. Subsection 1 refers to a 'qualifying business' while subsection 5(d) defines 'qualified business'; the document uses both terms. Subsection 5(e)(3) requires completion or substantial refurbishment after December 31, 2020. Predecessor section 57-39.2-04.13 (expired under S.L. 2015, ch. 456, § 3) covers a similar data center exemption; the text does not link the two.

thresholds.variable_text: aggregate floor area of the buildings containing the qualified data center
thresholds.value_text: an aggregate amount of fifteen thousand square feet [1394 square meters] or more
thresholds.measurement: Aggregate square footage of the buildings whose primary purpose is to contain a data center; office, meeting, mechanical and other support space counts if used to support the enterprise IT equipment (subsection 6)
thresholds.consequence: A facility meets this size element of the qualified data center definition only at or above this area.
thresholds.conditions: Also requires that no fewer than fifty percent of the floor area is used for data processing, a single or contiguous parcel, construction completed after December 31, 2020, certification by the tax commissioner, and the security attributes in subdivision e(4).

evidence.quote: consisting of an aggregate amount of fifteen thousand square feet [1394 square meters] or more

thresholds.variable_text: share of floor area of the qualified data center used for data processing
thresholds.value_text: no fewer than fifty percent of which is used for data processing
thresholds.measurement: Share of the buildings' floor area used for data processing; subsection 6 counts support space that supports the enterprise IT equipment
thresholds.consequence: A facility meets this element of the qualified data center definition only if at least this share of its buildings is used for data processing.
thresholds.conditions: Applies together with the 15,000 square foot aggregate size test in the same paragraph.

evidence.quote: no fewer than fifty percent of which is used for data processing

thresholds.variable_text: floor area rebuilt, modified or improved in a data center to make it substantially refurbished
thresholds.value_text: fifteen thousand square feet [1394 square meters] or more has been rebuilt, modified, or improved
thresholds.measurement: Aggregate floor area rebuilt, modified or improved through energy efficiency, building improvements, installation of enterprise IT equipment, environmental controls and computer software
thresholds.consequence: A data center meets the substantial refurbishment test, and a refurbished facility can then qualify as a qualified data center, only if at least this area is rebuilt, modified or improved.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to the definition of substantially refurbished in subdivision f.

evidence.quote: fifteen thousand square feet [1394 square meters] or more has been rebuilt, modified, or improved

thresholds.variable_text: date after which construction is completed or substantial refurbishment occurs
thresholds.measurement: Date of completion of construction or of substantial refurbishment of the facility
thresholds.consequence: Only facilities whose construction is completed, or which are substantially refurbished, after December 31, 2020 qualify as a qualified data center.
thresholds.conditions: Date cut-off stated as 31 December 2020; the operator is applied to the calendar year.

"Computer software" includes software used or loaded at a qualified data center, software maintenance, software licensing, and software customization.
"Data center" means a centralized repository for the storage, management, and dissemination of electronic data and information organized around a particular body or bodies of knowledge.
"Enterprise information technology equipment" includes:
"Qualified business" means the owner, operator, or tenants of a qualified data center.
"Qualified data center" means a newly constructed or substantially refurbished facility located in this state:
"Substantially refurbished" means a data center used to house enterprise information technology equipment

enforcement.note: Section 57-39.2-04.17 contains no penalty, fine, criminal sanction, licence or permit revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provision. Subsection 2 says an applicant's application may no longer be considered if it does not respond to a request for information within thirty days; this is an eligibility consequence and is not coded as enforcement. The section does not cross-reference the chapter's penalty provisions (57-39.2-18), and the exemption-disallowance language in 57-39.2-04.19 is in a different section.
